q1_triangulation_geometry.query: Setup: a tabletop 6-DOF robot arm (AgileX PiPER, about 0.63 m reach, fingertips reach about 0.76 m at table height) on a 1.29 x 1.36 m table against a wall. We want fixed RGB cameras (Raspberry Pi Camera Module 3 Wide, 102 x 67 deg field of view, 4608 x 2592 px) that (a) triangulate the gripper fingertips to check the arm's joint-angle kinematics (detect drift of a few mm), (b) show whether the workspace is clear, and (c) may later feed learned visuomotor policies. Current proposal: one camera about 1.2 m above the table looking straight down, one about 0.8 m from the arm base past the table end the arm faces at joint 1 = 0, about 0.42 m up and tilted 19 deg down, and a third low camera on the room-side table edge looking toward the wall. What do the close-range photogrammetry and multi-view computer vision literatures say about: (1) the optimal intersection (convergence) angle between camera rays for minimizing 3D triangulation error, and how fast the error grows when the angle falls below about 30-60 deg or rises above about 120 deg; (2) whether one near-vertical (nadir) camera plus two low oblique side cameras is a strong network for 3D point accuracy, compared with, for example, three cameras all elevated 30-45 deg and spread about 120 deg apart in azimuth; (3) how baseline, camera-to-target distance and pixel resolution set the depth error; and (4) how self-occlusion by the arm should change the number and spread of cameras (e.g. optimal camera placement for motion capture with occlusion). Give quantitative rules of thumb with citations.

q2_robot_learning_viewpoints.query: Setup: a tabletop 6-DOF robot arm (AgileX PiPER, about 0.63 m reach, fingertips reach about 0.76 m at table height) on a 1.29 x 1.36 m table against a wall. We want fixed RGB cameras (Raspberry Pi Camera Module 3 Wide, 102 x 67 deg field of view, 4608 x 2592 px) that (a) triangulate the gripper fingertips to check the arm's joint-angle kinematics (detect drift of a few mm), (b) show whether the workspace is clear, and (c) may later feed learned visuomotor policies. Current proposal: one camera about 1.2 m above the table looking straight down, one about 0.8 m from the arm base past the table end the arm faces at joint 1 = 0, about 0.42 m up and tilted 19 deg down, and a third low camera on the room-side table edge looking toward the wall. Which fixed third-person camera viewpoints do tabletop robot-manipulation datasets and benchmarks use (for example ALOHA / ALOHA 2, Mobile ALOHA, DROID, BridgeData V2, robomimic, FurnitureBench, RH20T, Open X-Embodiment, LeRobot SO-100/SO-101, AgileX Cobot Magic), including camera heights, distances and angles where reported, and what quantitative evidence exists on how viewpoint choice (overhead/top-down, front, side, over-the-shoulder) and the number of fixed views affect visuomotor policy success and robustness to camera shifts? Does the evidence support or contradict an overhead camera plus two side cameras?

q3_vision_calibration_accuracy.query: Setup: a tabletop 6-DOF robot arm (AgileX PiPER, about 0.63 m reach, fingertips reach about 0.76 m at table height) on a 1.29 x 1.36 m table against a wall. We want fixed RGB cameras (Raspberry Pi Camera Module 3 Wide, 102 x 67 deg field of view, 4608 x 2592 px) that (a) triangulate the gripper fingertips to check the arm's joint-angle kinematics (detect drift of a few mm), (b) show whether the workspace is clear, and (c) may later feed learned visuomotor policies. Current proposal: one camera about 1.2 m above the table looking straight down, one about 0.8 m from the arm base past the table end the arm faces at joint 1 = 0, about 0.42 m up and tilted 19 deg down, and a third low camera on the room-side table edge looking toward the wall. For checking or calibrating the kinematic accuracy of a low-cost serial robot arm with fixed external cameras and a fiducial (ArUco, AprilTag or ChArUco board, or a sphere) on the end effector, what camera distances, viewing angles and numbers of cameras have given the best end-effector position accuracy, what accuracies (mm) were achieved, and how does the viewing angle of a planar fiducial (frontal vs oblique) affect its pose and depth accuracy? Does the evidence favour two or more cameras at large angular separation over a single camera?

q4_pi_multicamera_sync.query: Has anyone built a multi-camera 3D tracking, motion-capture or photogrammetry system from Raspberry Pi cameras in which either several cameras share one Raspberry Pi through CSI ribbon cables of about 0.5 m or longer, or each camera has its own Raspberry Pi synchronized over the network (NTP, PTP or a hardware trigger), and what frame-synchronization accuracy, cable-length limits or signal-integrity problems were reported?
